title: Strings and Lists
overview:
Strings and lists are two of the most important data structures in Python. Strings hold text, while lists hold ordered collections of values.

Learning goals:
- strings
- indexing
- slicing
- lists
- list methods

Why it matters:
Most programs work with text and collections of values. Lists and strings are everyday tools for solving coding problems.

Example:
word = "python"
print(word[0])
print(word[0:3])
items = [1, 2, 3]
items.append(4)
print(items)

Think about this:
How is a list different from a string?
exercises: Print the first and last letter of a word.
Create a list of three fruits and print the second item.
